candidates.title: How To Do A SMITH MACHINE SHRUG | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide
candidates.description:
The Standing Smith Machine Shrug is an exercise that targets the muscles in the trapezius, aka, the traps.
► Try Our Workout App For Free: https://bit.ly/3ZNj7kv

Since the barbell on the smith machine moves in a locked in straight up and down path, it requires less activation of the stabilization muscles, thus making it easier to isolate the muscles in the trapezius.

To get started:
1. With a shoulder width stance, grip the barbell in front of your thighs, with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder width.
2. Lift the bar up off the rack with a slight backward twist to move the safety hooks away from the safety bar. 
3. Ensure you keep your shoulders back with your chest up.
4. While keeping your arms extended at your sides, elevate your shoulders as high as you can, without using your biceps.
5. The movement is only from the shoulders.
6. Pause to feel the contraction at the top, then under control, slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
7. Repeat for reps.

Smith Machine Shrug:
► MUSCLES WORKED: Trapezius, Shoulders
► TYPE: Strength
► EQUIPMENT: Smith Machine
► EXPERIENCE: Intermediate

candidates.title: ❌ 1 Barbell Shrug Mistake (FIX THIS)
candidates.description:
If you want to build bigger traps, you need to make sure you're using proper shrugs form during your back workouts. One common barbell shrug mistake is using too wide of a grip. This reduces your ability to build upper traps since it doesn't optimally line the resistance up with those fibers. Instead, when performing this back exercise make sure to use a wider grip a few inches outside of shoulder width. You'll build your upper trapezius more effectively this way.
